item.title: Go Daily Question 20250518
item.description:
Will the following code compile? If so, what will be the output?

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    s1 := []int{1, 2, 3}
    s2 := []int{4, 5}
    s1 = append(s1, s2)
    fmt.Println(s1)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Run online

Cannot compile. The second argument of append() cannot directly use a slice; it requires the ... operator to append one slice to another: append(s1, s2...). Alternatively, elements can be appended directly, such as: append(s1, 1, 2, 3).

item.title: Go Daily Question 193
item.description:
What do the following two code snippets output?

// 1.
func main() {
    s := make([]int, 5)
    s = append(s, 1, 2, 3)
    fmt.Println(s)
}

// 2.
func main() {
    s := make([]int,0)
    s = append(s,1,2,3,4)
    fmt.Println(s)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis: 
// 1.
[0 0 0 0 0 1 2 3]

// 2.
[1 2 3 4]

Reference analysis: This question tests appending elements to a slice using append. A common mistake for the first code snippet is expecting [1 2 3]; pay attention.

item.title: Go Daily Question 187
item.description:
Can data be appended to a nil slice?

🔑 Answer Analysis:

It depends on the declaration. If declared as var a []int = nil, then data can be appended. If declared as var a *[]int = nil, then it cannot.

item.title: Go Daily Question 102
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

func change(s ...int) {
    s = append(s,3)
}

func main() {
    slice := make([]int,5,5)
    slice[0] = 1
    slice[1] = 2
    change(slice...)
    fmt.Println(slice)
    change(slice[0:2]...)
    fmt.Println(slice)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis: 
[1 2 0 0 0]
[1 2 3 0 0]

Key takeaways: variadic functions, append() operation.

Go’s syntactic sugar ... allows passing a slice into a variadic function without creating a new slice. When change() is called the first time, the append() operation causes the underlying array of the slice to reallocate (grow), and the original slice’s underlying array remains unchanged. When change() is called the second time, a new slice, let’s call it slice1, is obtained using the operator [i:j]. Its underlying array overlaps with the original slice’s underlying array. However, slice1’s length and capacity are 2 and 5 respectively, so modifications to slice1’s underlying array within the change() function will affect the original slice.

item.title: Go Daily Question 098
item.description:
Will the following code terminate normally?

func main() {
    v := []int{1, 2, 3}
    for i := range v {
        v = append(v, i)
    }
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

It will not result in an infinite loop and will terminate normally.

The number of iterations is determined before the loop starts. Changing the length of the slice within the loop does not affect the number of iterations.
